STOP taking 20g of collagen in one shot 🛑 If you're dumping 2 scoops of Vital Proteins in your coffee every morning, you're wasting half of it. Here's why 👇 Collagen synthesis is SLOW and steady. The smarter way: **7-10g, 3 times a day.** Why it works better: • **Steady supply** — smaller doses keep collagen peptides (glycine, proline, hydroxyproline) circulating all day, so your skin, joints, and gut lining always have building blocks available • **Better absorption** — a moderate dose gets taken up more completely instead of overwhelming digestion in one hit • **Less bloat** — one giant scoop is why collagen makes some people feel heavy and gassy • **Matches how your body builds** — you wouldn't eat all your protein in one meal, and collagen is no different Morning coffee: 1 scoop. Afternoon smoothie or tea: 1 scoop. Evening: 1 scoop. Same total collagen — WAY better results. Your body doesn't need a flood. Collagen is what gives skin its structure, firmness, and bounce. And while we naturally make less of it as we age, there are ways to support what we have and encourage new production: - Vitamin C: An essential cofactor your body actually needs to synthesize and stabilize collagen. - Sun protection: UV exposure activates enzymes that break down collagen and contributes to photoaging. Protecting your skin helps preserve the collagen you already have. - Collagen generators: I use BioSil, a stabilized form of orthosilicic acid (ch-OSA). Human studies suggest it can support the body’s own collagen production and improve measures of skin elasticity and texture. - Red light therapy: Specific wavelengths of red/NIR light can influence cellular signaling and fibroblast activity, with studies showing improvements in collagen density and skin appearance. Wavelength and dose matter, which is why I prioritize quality devices. - Adequate protein: Collagen is a protein. Your body needs amino acids, especially glycine, proline  and lysine, as the raw materials to build it.
